evidence: Workflows (devflow.yml:1004, devflow-implement.yml:533, devflow-retrospective.yml:321) project claude_model from .prflow/config.json (or .github config via jq in security-audit.yml:38) and guard it with an allowlist (devflow.yml:1169-1172) before composing claude_args. No workflow reads devflow_retrospective.retrospective_model or audit_model (grep over .github finds them only in project-config.yml:94-95; comment at lines 88-91 says they are consumed by the local /devflow-weekly skill), so that part of the claim is wrong in scope. Whether 'claude-opus-5-5' is a model id the Claude action accepts cannot be established from source; no requirement shown broken.

project-config.yml:57-61 says 'medium' causes the workflow to omit --effort for the Claude-action workflows (claude/claude_implement/claude_runner). But devflow.yml:1175-1188, the claude_args builder, accepts medium and appends '--effort $EFFORT' whenever EFFORT_SUPPORTED=true and EFFORT is non-empty, so medium is passed explicitly. The same holds in devflow-implement.yml:711-716 and devflow-retrospective.yml:436-441. Only security-audit.yml:174 omits the flag for medium, and that section has its own comment. The comment is wrong for the workflows it sits above.

The workflow sets ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL as step env on anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 (security-audit.yml:73-76). Whether the action and the Claude Code CLI honour these variables depends on the external action and CLI source or docs, which are not in the supplied artifacts, and I did not run anything. My recollection is that the CLI documents them as overrides for the opus and sonnet aliases, not as a direct model selector. Whether that selects the audit model also depends on which alias the run resolves to. Neither point can be confirmed from the repository.

examples/sqlite-demo/sqllens.toml:16 sets model = "claude-opus-5-5". The repo only passes the string through to the Anthropic SDK, and nothing in it validates model ids. Whether the Anthropic API accepts this id needs the live Anthropic model list, which I did not have. The repo's own docs and tests use the same id, but they are not an authority on what the API accepts.

pyproject.toml:31 pins anthropic>=0.49,<1. In llm.py the adapter uses only messages.stream, stream.text_stream, get_final_message (lines 107-112), block.model_dump(mode=json, exclude_unset=True) (line 257), getattr on block.type, and extra_body for effort (241). It does not consume thinking/signature stream events directly, so the claim's premise that these features need 0.49 is not shown by the code; thinking blocks are only round-tripped as dumped dicts. Whether 0.49 is the true minimum and whether the whole <1 range is compatible depends on the Anthropic SDK changelog and release contents, which are not in the supplied artifacts, and I did not run the code against SDK versions.

LLMConfig.model default is claude-opus-5-5 (config.py:105); CLI installer --model default (cli.py:368) and generated TOML (cli.py:605) use it; mcpb manifest model default (manifest.json:68) and examples/sqlite-demo/sqllens.toml:16 use it. Adapter stores provider_content incl. thinking blocks (llm.py:253-259) and replays it for assistant messages, keeping thinking only for the current turn (llm.py:150-157), i.e. preserved across tool rounds. Overrides: model is a plain settings field and manifest passes SQLLENS_LLM__MODEL env, so TOML/env overrides win over the default. Counter-input considered: older-turn thinking is dropped, but the claim says across tool rounds, which holds.

llm.py _build_payload:141-157: last_user = index of last role=='user' message; for assistant messages with provider_content at i < last_user, only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks are filtered, keeping text/tool_use blocks (_provider_content:253-259 copies all blocks). Tool results are role 'tool', so they do not advance last_user; later tool requests within the same turn keep the same cutoff, so earlier-turn thinking stays omitted. Current-turn thinking (i > last_user) is retained, matching the doc. Trace of a hostile input: a prior-turn assistant message with thinking+tool_use yields tool_use only; a thinking-only message is dropped (no text/tool history lost).

Head view: config.py:105 LLMConfig.model default claude-opus-5-5 (max_tokens default 8192 at :110); cli.py:368 installer --model default and cli.py:605 generated config; mcpb/manifest.json:68; examples/sqlite-demo/sqllens.toml:16; anthropic/llm.py:54 adapter default (env override only when ANTHROPIC_MODEL set, explicit model takes precedence) and llm.py:233 falls back to 8192 when request.max_tokens is None. No other claude model defaults in these files.

Storage and carry-through hold: anthropic/llm.py:91 (non-streaming) and :119/:124 (streaming) set provider_content from _provider_content (:253, exclude_unset dump keeps empty thinking and signatures, block order kept); agent.py:1455-1472 accumulates it for streaming, agent.py:699/1108/1287 store it in Message and pass it to LlmMessage. But the claim that _build_payload 'replays them unchanged' is false for earlier turns. llm.py:150-155: when an assistant message index i < last_user, deepcopy'd provider_content has all thinking and redacted_thinking blocks filtered out (comment: 'never older signatures'), and the message is skipped entirely if nothing remains (:156). So in any multi-turn conversation, prior-turn thinking blocks and signatures are not replayed, contradicting the doc text 'replays them unchanged' and 'preserves empty thinking blocks, signatures' (docs/internal/agent/factory.md:58). The behavior may be intentional, but the doc omits the stripping qualifier.

factory.md:62 says effort goes via extra_body because SDK at the anthropic>=0.49 floor is 'not known to accept' an output_config kwarg. llm.py:238-241 in _build_payload does exactly this: payload['extra_body'] = {'output_config': {'effort': request.effort}}, with no output_config kwarg anywhere in the file. The claim is hedged ('not known'), so it asserts no SDK fact that could be contradicted. I did not inspect the SDK 0.49 source. Input traced: effort set to any level goes only through extra_body.

llm.py:252-259 _provider_content calls block.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_unset=True) over msg.content (dicts deepcopied). The claim concerns anthropic SDK behavior (pydantic fields_set for thinking signature/tool_use input, especially on stream.get_final_message() accumulated blocks, at the >=0.49 floor). pyproject.toml:31 pins "anthropic>=0.49,<1", matching the docstring (llm.py:5) and comment (llm.py:239) floor of 0.49. Thinking blocks and signature_delta arrived with Claude 3.7 support (SDK 0.47, Feb 2025), and extra_body is a long-standing per-request option, so 0.49 covers all three. This SDK-history part comes from my knowledge, not from anything in the repo.

Producer _provider_content (llm.py:253-259) returns only dicts (deepcopy of dict or model_dump(mode='json')). Consumers store it in pydantic fields typed Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] (storage/models.py:25, llm/models.py:26,56,70), so rehydration/validation rejects non-dict elements before _build_payload's block.get at llm.py:154-155. agent.py passes msg.provider_content through unchanged (1287).

llm.py:150-159 replays provider_content only, skipping content/tool_calls. provider_content is built by _provider_content (llm.py:253-259) from every block of the same Anthropic message (llm.py:91, 119, 124), including tool_use blocks. The tool_calls are parsed from that same message (llm.py:114, _parse_message_content 277+), so tool_use ids are identical. agent.py:695-700 stores both tool_calls and provider_content from the same response. The tool branch (llm.py:161-182) builds tool_result blocks from tool_call_id. Only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks are filtered (llm.py:152-155), and those are never tool_use. So every tool_use id is preserved. The one input I traced was a streaming response with tool calls and an older-turn thinking filter. In both, the tool_use blocks remain.

llm.py:141-157: last_user is the max index of role=='user' messages; tool results use role 'tool' (llm.py:161-182) so they do not count as user turns. Assistant provider_content before last_user has thinking/redacted_thinking blocks stripped; those at or after it (the current tool-use turn) keep them intact. This matches Anthropic's extended-thinking rule: thinking blocks must be passed back unmodified during the current assistant turn's tool-use loop, while earlier turns' thinking blocks may be omitted (the API ignores or strips them).

llm.py:58-64 copies **extra_client_kwargs into client_kwargs and passes them to anthropic.Anthropic(**client_kwargs), so http_client is forwarded unchanged. anthropic.Anthropic's http_client parameter is a sync httpx.Client (the sync client uses self._client.messages.stream, llm.py:107, inside an async generator). tests/unit/test_opus_history.py:116-120 passes a sync httpx.Client with MockTransport and consumes stream_request. I did not run the test or read the installed anthropic source.
llm.py:233 fallback is 8192; config.py:109-110 LLMConfig.max_tokens default=8192; factory.py:175 passes cfg.llm.max_tokens into the request. Values match.

anthropic/llm.py:108-125: text chunks (line 110) carry only content; exactly one final chunk (either branch, lines 116-125) carries provider_content=self._provider_content(final), built from the final message. agent.py:1455-1456 keeps last non-None value, so it equals the complete final block list.

storage/models.py:20 Message.content is a plain str with no non-empty validator, and provider_content is Optional (line 25); conversation_store.py and local/storage.py do no content validation. agent.py:1103-1110 stores such a message. _build_llm_request (agent.py:1282-1287) copies content and provider_content unchanged. The only LlmService in src is AnthropicLlmService. It handles an assistant message with provider_content at llm.py:150-159 by emitting the provider blocks, and skips the turn if no blocks remain, so no empty-text turn is emitted. filter/base.py:37 uses `msg.content or ''`. No non-Anthropic payload builder exists in src to break.

storage/models.py:25 declares provider_content as Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] on a pydantic Message, which round-trips through model_dump or JSON as list of dicts. The only ConversationStore implementations (conversation_store.py:39 BoundedConversationStore and integrations/local/storage.py:14 MemoryConversationStore) keep Conversation objects in in-process dicts and never serialize, so the field is preserved by reference with signatures intact. agent.py:1287 copies msg.provider_content when rebuilding messages.

llm.py:70 calls self._client.messages.create(**payload) synchronously and uses the result as a Message; llm.py:107-112 uses a sync `with self._client.messages.stream(**payload) as stream`, iterates stream.text_stream and calls stream.get_final_message(). The fake (test_opus_history.py:32-63) has a sync create returning a validated anthropic Message, and stream returning a sync context manager with text_stream and get_final_message. This matches the sync Anthropic client surface the service uses.

_BLOCKS (test_opus_history.py:21-25) is fed via Message.model_validate (line 37). _provider_content (llm.py:253-259) dumps with model_dump(mode='json', exclude_unset=True), so SDK defaulted fields (e.g. text block citations=None) that were not in the input are not emitted. Every field in _BLOCKS (type, thinking incl. empty string, signature, text, id, name, input) is explicitly set, so it is retained, including the empty thinking text. The first-round tool id is tool-1, matching _BLOCKS. The equality at line 85 therefore compares like with like. I did not execute the test.

The anthropic SDK source (lib/streaming, raw_*_event models) is not in the head view, so I could not check the schema against the pinned version. I did not run the test.

llm.py:150-159 _build_payload deep-copies provider_content and strips thinking/redacted_thinking only when i < last_user (index of last role=='user' message). Tool results use role 'tool' (llm.py:161), so they do not advance last_user. Every assistant message within the current tool round (after the last user message) is replayed unchanged. Stripping happens only for turns before the latest user turn, which is a different case from a tool round. Hostile input traced: a multi-user-turn history with an assistant+tool loop after the final user message. Its blocks are all kept intact, and only earlier-turn thinking is dropped. The comment at models.py:25 therefore holds for tool rounds.

tests/unit/test_opus_history.py:4 docstring is accurate. The real agent loop (_agent/_run) drives a tool round. With a fake messages client, the second request's assistant content equals _BLOCKS exactly (lines 83-86), covering thinking signature, order and tool input. Lines 89-122 additionally run the real SDK stream parser over mocked SSE and retain the signature and tool input. Hostile input: a follow-up turn drops old thinking (lines 150-157), but that is a different turn, not a tool round. Within the current turn's round the blocks are kept (line 155). The fake client bypasses only HTTP serialization for two of the tests, and the docstring does not claim otherwise.

llm.py:253-259 _provider_content uses model_dump(mode='json', exclude_unset=True) on blocks from messages.create (line 70) and stream.get_final_message (line 112). Whether stream-accumulated blocks (anthropic.lib.streaming accumulate_event, which mutates blocks via setattr/+=) keep every wire field in model_fields_set for every block type could not be checked: the SDK source is not in the supplied views and a filesystem search timed out.
